page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.re6p.xlarge is a virtualization instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor based on the x86_64 architecture. The host allocates 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz with hyperthreading enabled. Memory configuration totals 16.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:4 ratio of vCPUs to system memory. The processor subsystem includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 35 MB of shared L3 cache, with hardware instruction support for AVX-512 and AVX-512 VNNI vector operations.

Storage and connectivity rely strictly on attached infrastructure, as the instance includes no local disk storage. Operating systems and application data must be hosted on external block storage volumes. Network connectivity is rated at a 2 Gbps baseline bandwidth, with no complimentary public IPv4 addresses included. In addition, the configuration contains no discrete GPU acceleration, directing all computational demands to the host CPU cores.

Synthetic benchmarking via stress-ng reveals measured values of 1317.6 for single-core execution and 3505.41 for multi-core throughput, both aligning with the bottom quartile of contemporary cloud performance tiers. Consequently, the hardware profile is suited for moderate general-purpose workloads rather than high-performance computing. Common operational use cases include lightweight web application hosting, mid-tier microservices, development environments, and small relational databases with modest query intensity.

The server provides 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio with 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware capabilities include 35 MB of L3 cache alongside support for AVX-512 and AVX-512 VNNI instruction sets. The instance includes no local storage or discrete GPU accelerators, operating with external network storage and a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile. Benchmark results in stress-ng yield scores of 1317.6 in single-core and 3505.41 in multi-core testing, positioning its compute throughput within the lower performance quartile. As a result, ecs.re6p.xlarge provides balanced capacity for moderate operational tasks, small transactional databases, light web services, and background batch processing jobs that prioritize balanced resource distribution over intensive compute cycles.
